title: Guitar Theory: Summary and Reference
intro: Everything from the guitar lessons on one page, for looking things up while you play. No sound examples here: each section links back to its lesson.

items: Standard tuning, low to high: E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4 (strings 6 to 1). Neighbouring strings are a fourth (5 frets) apart, except G–B, a major third (4 frets).
Each fret is one semitone. Fret 12 is an octave above the open string; the pattern repeats from there.
Octave shapes: from strings 6 or 5, two strings up and two frets higher; from strings 4 or 3, two strings up and three frets higher; string 6 and string 1 at the same fret are two octaves apart.
Same pitch on the next thicker string: 5 frets higher (4 when going from the B string to the G string). Lesson: Notes on the Fretboard (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/fretboard).

major 2nd       +2            -
minor 3rd       +3            2 frets back
major 3rd       +4            1 fret back
perfect 4th     +5            same fret
tritone         +6            1 fret up
perfect 5th     +7            2 frets up
                              two strings up:
major 6th                     1 fret back
minor 7th                     same fret
major 7th                     1 fret up
octave          +12           2 frets up
Crossing G to B: add one fret on the B string.

items: Root: the note the chord is named after and built on; on the guitar usually the lowest string you strum (Roots (#/arts/music-theory/chords/roots)).
E-shape barre (root on string 6 under finger 1): major 1-3-3-2-1-1, minor 1-3-3-1-1-1, 7 1-3-1-2-1-1, m7 1-3-1-1-1-1 (shown at fret 1 = F).
A-shape barre (root on string 5 under finger 1): major x-1-3-3-3-1, minor x-1-3-3-2-1, 7 x-1-3-1-3-1, m7 x-1-3-1-2-1 (at fret 1 = B♭).
Power chord: root + fifth (+ octave), e.g. G5 = 3-5-5-x-x-x. No third, so neither major nor minor.
Triads on the top three strings (C major): x-x-x-5-5-3, x-x-x-9-8-8, x-x-x-12-13-12.
Shells (root, 3rd, 7th): G7 3-x-3-4-x-x, Cmaj7 x-3-2-4-x-x, Dm7 x-5-3-5-x-x.
Major vs minor: lower the chord's third by one fret. Lesson: Chords (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/chord-voicings).
A minor pentatonic, box 1 (frets 5–8): string 6: 5, 8 · 5: 5, 7 · 4: 5, 7 · 3: 5, 7 · 2: 5, 8 · 1: 5, 8. Roots A at string 6 fret 5, string 4 fret 7, string 1 fret 5.
Blues scale: add the ♭5 (string 5 fret 6 in A).
Move the box: put finger 1 on the new root on string 6 (G at 3, C at 8, E at 0 or 12).
Relative major: the same box is C major pentatonic.
G major, second position (frets 2–5): string 6: 2 3 5 · 5: 2 3 5 · 4: 2 4 5 · 3: 2 4 5 · 2: 3 5 · 1: 2 3 5.
Modes: same pattern, different home note (A = Dorian, D = Mixolydian in G major). Lesson: Scales (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/scales).
Order up the neck: C → A → G → E → D → C (octave).
C major: C shape x32010, A shape x-3-5-5-5-3, G shape 8-7-5-5-5-8, E shape 8-10-10-9-8-8, D shape x-x-10-12-13-12.
Root strings: E shape strings 6, 4 and 1; A shape strings 5 and 3; C shape strings 5 and 2; D shape strings 4 and 2; G shape strings 6, 3 and 1. Lesson: CAGED (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/caged).

Common progressions:  1-4-5-1   1-5-6m-4   6m-4-1-5   1-6m-4-5
Minor:                i-bVII-bVI-V (Am-G-F-E)
12-bar blues:         1 1 1 1 | 4 4 1 1 | 5 4 1 5
Capo: shapes sound N semitones higher with the capo at fret N.

items: Safe notes: the minor pentatonic of the key (A minor pentatonic over an A blues).
Strong notes: the chord tones of the chord underneath, especially its third and seventh; end phrases on the root.
Guide tones: thirds and sevenths move by a semitone or stay put as the chords change (A7 → D7: C♯ → C).
Bends: check the target pitch on the fret two above for a whole-step bend. Lesson: Soloing over Chords (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/soloing).
